nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator who runs the recovery CLIs (es-merge, es-generate, demo) and launches es-view. Here they invoke es-generate to render the merged model into the DOT graph and the interactive explorer.

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process boundary. Holds the merged flows.json read as input and receives the generated view artifacts (flows.dot + explorer.html) written into the output directory.

tactical.explanation: Reached via node:fs. generate-views reads the model with fs.readFileSync(flowsFile) and writes both artifacts with fs.writeFileSync into <outDir>: flows.dot and explorer.html. These are plain files on disk, not a database.

anchors.note: readFileSync(flowsFile) — reads flows.json
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot)
writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html)

nodes.label: Local editor (VS Code)
nodes.description: The developer's local editor, outside the process boundary. Both generated artifacts embed vscode://file/... deep links so that clicking a sticky's source anchor opens the exact file and line in the editor.

tactical.explanation: Links are built by anchorUrl, which is defined twice with identical form: once for the DOT side (node URLs) and once inside the inlined SPA (detail-panel anchors). Both produce `vscode://file/${repoRoot}/${a.path}:${a.line}`. Whether the link resolves depends entirely on repoRoot being an absolute path (see hot-unresolved-repo-root-links).

anchors.note: DOT-side vscode:// URL builder
SPA-side vscode:// URL builder (inlined into explorer.html)

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Built by the merge, then read by the es-view server and by this view generator. Its invariants are the merge-time validations.

tactical.explanation: In this flow the model is a READ-ONLY input: generate-views JSON.parses flows.json into `model` (line 24) and builds a nodeById / hotspotById index (30-31) plus a DATA_TYPES filter (36-37). The generator never mutates or re-validates the aggregate; it only projects it into views. meta.repoRoot and meta.title act as fallbacks for the --repo-root / --title flags (27-28).

anchors.note: JSON.parse(readFileSync(flowsFile)) — the model is the generator's input
index nodes + hotspots for lookup during rendering

nodes.label: GenerateViews
nodes.description: Render the merged model into its human-facing views: a Graphviz DOT board and a self-contained interactive explorer. A pure read-side ETL/transform — it reads the model and emits view artifacts, changing no domain state.

tactical.explanation: ETL transform kept on a single plane per the two-plane rule; NONE of its internal stages are promoted to aggregates/policies/events. (1) Parse argv: flowsFile, outDir, and the --repo-root / --title flags with meta fallbacks (19-28). (2) Read the model and index it (24, 30-37). (3) BUILD DOT (62-90): emit `digraph event_storming` with one `subgraph cluster_<flowId>` per flow; within each, the used node set is steps + edge endpoints MINUS any physical node (server/database/table/column) and any edge touching one (isDataId, 37,73-74); each behavioral node becomes a filled+rounded box colored from PALETTE (fill/edge/text), the node's FIRST tactical anchor becomes a vscode:// URL (78-79), and dead/superseded flows render dashed with a [STATUS] label (69-71,81). Write flows.dot (91). (4) BUILD explorer.html (93-1486): assemble one large template string that inlines the entire model as `const MODEL = ${modelJson}` (438, with `<` escaped to \u003c at 94), plus `const REPO_ROOT` (439) and `const PALETTE` (440), followed by a dependency-free vanilla-JS SPA (flows board, gallery, data-model tab, glossary, detail panel with source anchors). Write explorer.html (1487) and log the two paths (1489). Both the DOT-building and HTML-templating stages stay in this tactical block; only the completed render is promoted (evt-views-generated).

anchors.note: argv: flowsFile, outDir, --repo-root, --title (+ meta fallbacks at 27-28)
reads the merged model (input to the transform)
DOT build: one subgraph per flow; physical nodes excluded (36-37,73-74)
explorer.html template string; MODEL/REPO_ROOT/PALETTE inlined at 438-440

nodes.label: Flows DOT graph
nodes.description: The Graphviz digraph (flows.dot): one cluster per flow with event-storming-colored stickies and labeled edges, rendered offline (e.g. `dot -Tsvg`) or in a Graphviz viewer to read the whole board at a glance. Physical storage nodes and any edge touching them are deliberately excluded.

tactical.explanation: Built by the DOT block (62-90) and written to <outDir>/flows.dot at line 91. Each flow is a `subgraph cluster_<flowId>`; the used-node set is steps + edge endpoints filtered through isDataId so server/database/table/column nodes never appear (37,73-74). Node ids are namespaced per flow as `<flowId>__<nodeId>` so a shared node repeats visually inside each flow that uses it. Colors come from PALETTE by node type; the first tactical anchor is attached as a vscode:// URL (78-79). Dead/superseded flows render with a dashed style and a [STATUS] suffix (69-71,81).

anchors.note: digraph header + per-flow subgraphs
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot)

nodes.label: Interactive explorer
nodes.description: The self-contained explorer.html read model: the entire model inlined as a JS constant plus a dependency-free vanilla-JS SPA (flows board, node gallery, data-model tab, glossary, and a detail panel with clickable source anchors). Opens directly in a browser with no server and no external assets.

tactical.explanation: Assembled as one template string (93-1486) and written to <outDir>/explorer.html at line 1487. The whole model is frozen into the page at line 438 (`const MODEL = ${modelJson}`, where modelJson is JSON.stringify(model) with `<` escaped to \u003c at line 94 to keep the inline <script> safe); REPO_ROOT and PALETTE are inlined at 439-440. The SPA rebuilds nodeById/hotspotById from MODEL (441-442) and constructs vscode:// deep links via its own anchorUrl (478), used across the detail panel (998,1410,1459). Because the model is embedded rather than fetched, the artifact is a FROZEN snapshot (see hot-frozen-explorer-snapshot) and is offline-safe (no <script src=> — asserted by the smoke test).

anchors.note: start of the explorer.html template string
entire model inlined as const MODEL (frozen snapshot)
writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html)

nodes.label: ViewsGenerated
nodes.description: The read-model views (flows.dot + explorer.html) have been rendered from the current model and written into the output directory, ready for a human to open, share, or feed to Graphviz. The single domain fact promoted out of the render pipeline.

tactical.explanation: Realized by the two fs.writeFileSync calls (91 for the DOT, 1487 for the HTML) and the closing console.log that reports both paths (1489). All intermediate DOT-building and HTML-templating stages stay inside cmd-generate-views tactical per the two-plane rule; this event is the only fact promoted from them. The generator has no failure/validation branch of its own here (an unparseable flows.json throws at read time, line 24); a successful run always emits exactly this fact.

anchors.note: flows.dot written
explorer.html written
console.log('wrote ... and ...') — both artifacts done

flows.name: Operator generates the DOT + explorer views from the model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-generate over a merged flows.json and an output directory. The tool reads the model once and projects it into two human-facing read models without mutating any domain state: a Graphviz DOT board (one cluster per flow, physical storage nodes excluded) and a self-contained explorer.html that inlines the whole model and a dependency-free SPA. Both artifacts are written to the output directory and embed vscode:// deep links back into the analyzed checkout. The point is to turn the abstract model into something a human can open in a browser or Graphviz and click straight to source.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node tools/generate-views.js <flows.json> <outDir> --repo-root <abs> --title "..."` (via the `es-generate` bin, or `npm run demo` -> scripts/build-example.mjs).

hotspots.label: explorer.html embeds a frozen model snapshot that silently drifts from flows.json
hotspots.description: The generator inlines the entire model into explorer.html as `const MODEL = ...` (line 438). Unlike the es-view server, which serves the live in-memory model, the generated explorer is a self-contained static COPY: once flows.json changes (a re-merge, a later data-mapping pass), an already-open or already-shared explorer.html keeps showing stale nodes/flows/terms until someone re-runs es-generate. Nothing in the artifact records which model version or commit it was built from. Human question: should the explorer stamp the source model's version / meta.generatedFrom (or a build timestamp) and surface a 'this snapshot may be stale' signal, or is a frozen, shareable, offline snapshot the intended contract that the reader is expected to keep regenerating?

tactical.explanation: modelJson = JSON.stringify(model) with `<` escaped to \u003c (94), then inlined verbatim at `const MODEL = ${modelJson}` (438). The SPA reads only from MODEL (441-442) — there is no fetch, no version banner, and no reference back to the on-disk flows.json. Contrast the es-view server, which holds the model in memory and re-resolves it. The smoke test even asserts the model is embedded and there are no external <script src=> tags, confirming the static/offline design is deliberate.

anchors.note: JSON.stringify(model), < escaped for inline <script>
whole model frozen into the page
static explorer.html written; no live source link

hotspots.label: vscode:// deep links silently break when --repo-root is not an absolute path
hotspots.description: Every source anchor becomes `vscode://file/${repoRoot}/${a.path}:${a.line}` (line 60 for DOT, line 478 in the SPA). repoRoot defaults to model.meta.repoRoot, and if that is absent, to '.' (line 27). But the vscode://file/ scheme requires an ABSOLUTE path, so when neither --repo-root nor meta.repoRoot is set the links become `vscode://file/./src/...` and silently open nothing. A set-but-wrong repoRoot (a different machine's checkout path) fails the same way, and nothing warns at generate time. Human question: should es-generate validate that repoRoot is an absolute, existing path (and warn/refuse otherwise), given that a broken deep link is indistinguishable to the viewer from a file that simply won't open?

tactical.explanation: repoRoot = argVal('--repo-root', (model.meta && model.meta.repoRoot) || '.') at line 27 — the '.' fallback is the trap. Both anchorUrl definitions (60 DOT-side, 478 SPA-side) interpolate repoRoot directly into a vscode://file/ URL with no absolute-path check or normalization. The DOT side additionally only ever links the FIRST anchor of each node (78-79), so secondary anchors are unreachable from the graph regardless of repoRoot.

anchors.note: defaults to meta.repoRoot else '.', no absolute-path validation
DOT-side vscode:// link built from raw repoRoot
SPA-side vscode:// link built from raw REPO_ROOT
